goals: Use the two laws of reflection
Describe the image in a plane mirror

cards.title: Light travels in straight lines
cards.body:
Light moves in straight lines. That's why an object in its path casts a sharp shadow.

When light hits a surface, some of it bounces back. This bouncing back is called **reflection**.

cards.title: The two laws of reflection

rows.value: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection
The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal all lie in the same plane
The line at 90° to the mirror where the ray hits it

cards.remember: Angles are always measured from the normal, not from the mirror.

cards.question: A ray strikes a plane mirror making an angle of 35° with the normal. What is the angle of reflection?
cards.why: Angles are measured from the normal. The angle of incidence is 35°, and by the first law of reflection the angle of reflection equals it: 35°. 55° is the angle with the mirror's surface, not with the normal.

cards.title: The image in a plane mirror

rows.value: Virtual: it can't be caught on a screen
As far behind the mirror as the object is in front
Laterally inverted: left and right swap

cards.title: Lateral inversion
cards.body:
Raise your right hand in front of a mirror and your image raises its left. This left–right swap is **lateral inversion**.

It's why AMBULANCE is written in reverse on the front of ambulances: drivers ahead read it the right way round in their mirrors.

cards.question: You stand 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far are you from your image?
cards.why: The image is as far behind the mirror as you are in front of it, so it's 2 m behind. The distance between you and your image is 2 m + 2 m = 4 m.

cards.title: Real and virtual images
cards.body:
A **real** image forms where light rays actually meet. It can be caught on a screen and is always inverted.

A **virtual** image forms where rays only seem to come from. It can't be caught on a screen.
cards.remember: A plane mirror always forms a virtual image.

cards.question: Which is true of the image formed by a plane mirror?
cards.why: A plane mirror's image can't be caught on a screen, so it's virtual, and it is always the same size as the object. Real, inverted images come from concave mirrors.

points: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface
Angle of incidence = angle of reflection, measured from the normal
A plane mirror's image is virtual, erect, the same size and laterally inverted
